text:
Predicates:
BredBack(x) ::: x is bred-back.
DomesticAnimal(x) ::: x is a domestic animal.
SelectiveBreeding(x) ::: x is subject to deliberate selective breeding.
HeckCattle(x) ::: x is Heck cattle.
Resemble(x, y) ::: x resembles y.
Aurochs(x) ::: x is an aurochs.
Extinct(x) ::: x is extinct.
Premises:
∀x (BredBack(x) → (SelectiveBreeding(x) ∧ DomesticAnimal(x))) ::: Breeding back is a form of artificial selection by the deliberate selective breeding of domestic animals.
HeckCattle(heck) ∧ BredBack(heck) ∧ Resemble(heck, aurochs) ∧ Resemble(aurochs, extinct) ::: Heck cattle were bred-back in the 1920s to resemble the aurochs.
Animals(heck) ∧ Animals(aurochs) ::: Heck cattle are animals. Aurochs are animals.
∃x (BredBack(x) ∧ Resemble(x, extinct)) ::: Some animals to be bred-back resemble animals that are extinct.
Conclusion:
∃x (HeckCattle(x) ∧ BredBack(x)) ::: Some Heck cattle are artificially selected.
